The space station orbited a desolate planet, its metallic corridors echoing with the solitary hum of machinery. Outside the viewing ports, a ballet of asteroids danced against the inky backdrop of space.

This desolate planet, known as Xylos Prime, was once a thriving hub of interstellar commerce during the Galactic Expansion Era of the 24th century. Its surface, now a barren wasteland of jagged rock and frozen methane lakes, was scarred by the catastrophic Resource Wars that tore the sector apart. The station itself, the *Aethelgard*, was constructed from recycled hull plating of ancient warships, a testament to the scarcity of raw materials in this remote corner of the galaxy. Its corridors, once bustling with traders and diplomats, now echoed only with the mechanical breath of life-support systems and the distant, rhythmic thrum of the fusion core. The "ballet of asteroids" outside was not merely a natural phenomenon; it was the debris field of a forgotten battle, a graveyard of ships that had tried to flee the planet's fall. The inky backdrop of space was punctuated by the faint, ghostly glow of nebulae, remnants of a star that had gone supernova centuries ago, casting long, eerie shadows across the station's observation deck. The air inside was thick with the scent of ozone and stale recycled oxygen, a constant reminder of the station's isolation and the fragility of human presence in the void.
